control_page.header_crc: CRC32 over the fixed 256-byte header with header_crc32 zeroed

flags.bit0: prefix_patched: current native-size ROM prefix differs from the recorded clean source and is authenticated by working_prefix_sha256

identity_policy.source_sha1_sha256: immutable identity of the validated retail ROM used to create the expanded image
identity_policy.working_prefix_sha256: hash of the current 8/16 MiB executable prefix after runtime patches
identity_policy.clean_expand: working_prefix_sha256 equals source_sha256 and prefix_patched is clear
identity_policy.runtime_patch: source identity remains unchanged; prefix_patched is set and working_prefix_sha256 is refreshed

relocation_directory.rule: Expanded tables and assets are registered here when relocation patchers are added; no later-generation IDs are preassigned by the container.
relocation_directory.allocation_policy: append from the highest registered end offset with explicit power-of-two alignment; never discover incidental free-space gaps
validation: directory names are unique 1..16 byte ASCII strings
allocations stay inside the common payload
fixed-stride entries may not declare count*stride larger than their allocation

payload.allocation_policy: explicit allocator/manifest only; do not scan incidental 0xFF gaps
payload.current_contents: allocator-ready; concrete table formats/contents are installed explicitly

invariants: A clean container build preserves the original native ROM prefix byte-for-byte.
The expanded image is exactly 32 MiB, the full directly addressable GBA ROM window.
All supported regions use the same control and payload addresses.
The Japanese 8 MiB image is padded to the common 16 MiB base; its original 8 MiB prefix is unchanged.
The control header records exact source SHA-1 and SHA-256 digests, game code and revision.
Generation 10 content IDs are not preassigned.
No ROM image is stored in the repository.
Relocation allocation is explicit and append-only from registered high water; unregistered 0xFF gaps are not reused.
Runtime patch stages may modify the executable prefix only after setting prefix_patched and refreshing working_prefix_sha256.
The original retail source SHA-1/SHA-256 identity remains immutable across runtime patch stages.
Verification checks the current prefix against working_prefix_sha256 and checks the immutable source identity against the known Sapphire ROM matrix.
